attrs.evidence: Fable 5 reconstructed the full promoted revision-name to OID mapping for the post-recovery chain from one read of refs/heads/invariant-canonical, walking parent.commit_oid through committed receipts, and GPT-5.6 independently reproduced it against the shipped INV-R8.3 bundle. scripts/check-publication-identity.mjs re-runs that walk at every head. The reader protocol matters and is part of the claim: git's multi-ref transaction is all-or-none in what it COMMITS, but a concurrent reader may still observe a subset of the changed refs, so a reader that combines a branch read with a tag read can see a mixed snapshot. Under the one-ref protocol subset visibility can stale a convenience index and cannot produce two identities for an OID already read.
attrs.gap: CONTENT-INTEGRITY-BOUND AND SELF-IDENTIFYING FROM THE OID HANDLE — NOT SELF-AUTHENTICATING, and the wrong word was in the Fable witness's own conclusion. A git OID content-binds an object under the hash assumption. It does not establish who produced it, whether the canonical ref was rolled back, whether an attacker replaced the whole repository or bundle, or whether the head is fresh. Those are FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH and remain open. Second, the minimality half is scoped to THIS publication interface: in a pull-based git design exposing a moving current head, one mutable canonical ref suffices for identity discovery — an append-only publication log or out-of-band immutable OID delivery is a counter-design, so the universal form Fable proposed is not claimed. Third: this is a PROTOCOL theorem, not a git theorem, and it binds only readers who follow the protocol.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's adjudication §2 and §3. SLSA Source v1.2 on logically immutable source revisions; git-update-ref(1) on committed-versus-observed ref state.
attrs.review_focus: The claim now rests on a declared observer protocol. Is the protocol stated precisely enough that a reader can tell whether they are following it — and is there anything in this artifact that reads a tag to establish identity?
attrs.statement: From the chain root onward the factory treats the canonical commit OID plus the committed receipt as authoritative source identity: a reader takes ONE ref read, uses the returned OID as an immutable handle, and derives revision identity from committed content without consulting the tag namespace.
